title: NexGen Cloud hires Nscale's Dan Thomas as chief infrastructure officer
html:
UK-based neocloud company NexGen Cloud has appointed former Nscale VP of AI infrastructure and operations Dan Thomas as its new chief infrastructure officer.

The company has also brought online its second European cloud region, dubbed EU2 and located in Oulu, Finland.

Thomas will be responsible for NexGen's infrastructure strategy and operations, including data center partnerships and site expansion, GPU cluster deployment and lifecycle, network and storage architecture, and its reliability, automation, and security practices.

Thomas will report to CEO and cofounder Chris Starkey and lead the company's infrastructure, site reliability, and network operations teams.

“Demand for sovereign AI compute in Europe is running ahead of supply, and the providers that win will be the ones that can bring large, reliable GPU capacity online fastest and run it to a standard that regulated customers can audit,” said CEO Starkey. “Dan has built and run infrastructure at exactly this scale. With EU1 fully reserved, EU2 coming online in Finland, and plans to deploy more than 20,000 GPUs across Europe next year, his job is to make sure every megawatt we add performs from day one. He is the right leader for this phase of the company.”

Thomas comes from fellow UK neocloud Nscale, which is currently preparing for an initial public offering (IPO) on the Nasdaq stock exchange.

Speaking to DCD exclusively on his decision to leave Nscale at such a pivotal time, Thomas said: "Nothing pushed me away from Nscale. If you look at my career trajectory, I've stayed at a couple of locations for a long time and did lots of roles at those places. I aspired to be C-suite; I've got a pretty unique skill set, and I felt that my capabilities, my expertise, and honestly, the battle scars that I carry... If I could go back and do things differently in certain ways, I would definitely have seen when I could have zagged with some of my operational decision-making, and having the opportunity to bring those lessons learned and provide that capability to NexGen and really help them execute on delivery was a genuinely attractive offer."

Commenting on NexGen specifically, Thomas noted that he thinks a "key distinguisher" in the neocloud market is going to be "the neoclouds that can deliver on what they say they can. That can get a cluster over to the customer on the date agreed, fully validated and ready for production. I think that's going to be exceedingly challenging.

"What I love about NexGen is that they are very pragmatic and very sensible, and they are very candid. When we are talking to customers, we are not promising what we can't deliver."

While this is not directly addressing any other company, these are questions investors are currently asking of neoclouds which have large remaining performance obligations, contracted power pipelines, and limited live capacity.

For example, Firmus has 900MW+ of contracted capacity and around 46MW live. Nscale, meanwhile, has 1.37GW of active and contracted capacity. In August, Nscale had 55MW spread across five data centers live, and as of recent documentation, it has seven sites live with an undisclosed capacity.

Firmus was previously set to IPO in Australia but had to pull out after receiving less investor interest than anticipated, with the company at the time blaming "market volatility." Nscale is still pursuing its own public offering.

Along with announcing Thomas' appointment at NexGen, the neocloud has also revealed that its cloud region in Oulu, Finland, has launched. Developed in partnership with Nordic cloud and data center operator GleSYS, EU2 will have thousands of GPUs across 8MW of capacity.

The region joins NexGen's existing cloud region in Falkenberg, Sweden, which reached full capacity in its first year of operation; the initial phase of EU2 was largely reserved ahead of launch. NexGen will reserve some of the region's capacity for its Hyperstack on-demand customers.

NexGen is planning to deploy more than 20,000 GPUs across Europe in 2027.

NexGen was founded in 2020, but launched its flagship platform, Hyperstack, in September 2023. In April 2025, the company raised $45 million in a Series A funding round. NexGen has previously declared plans to invest $1bn in an "AI supercloud."
summary: Also brings online cloud region in Finland
